hero.name: Ebrahim Abdelghfar Ebrahim
hero.title: Robotics Software Engineer
hero.bio: I write navigation and control software for mobile robots and autonomous vehicles, and build the simulators that test it before it goes into the field. Most of my work is C++ and Python on Linux, with ROS 2, Nav2, CARLA and Isaac Sim.

typewriterTexts: M.Sc. researcher in adaptive nonlinear MPC

experience.title: Robotics Simulation Engineer
details: Built the software-in-the-loop (SIL) pipeline in CARLA 0.9.16 and Unreal Engine 4.26, with realistic LiDAR, camera and GNSS models and vehicle dynamics. This cut on-site testing by 70%.
Set up a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) bench that feeds simulated sensor data to the vehicle in the formats its drivers expect, so the onboard stack runs against the simulator without changes.
Made a GUI tool on top of CARLA ScenarioRunner so the team can build automated test scenarios visually rather than coding each one.
Brought UAV-captured dense point clouds into CARLA through custom data pipelines to make the simulated environments more faithful.
Adapted NVIDIA Cosmos-Drive-Dreams to generate synthetic training data from CARLA scenes, helping the perception stack close the sim-to-real gap.

experience.title: Robotics Systems Engineer
details: Delivered the ROS 2 / Nav2 navigation stack for the company's mobile robot, combining cuVSLAM visual odometry with RTAB-Map occupancy-grid mapping. Localisation error stayed within 0.17 m over a ~1 km run.
Designed the Model Predictive Controller (MPC) for the four-wheel independent-steering robot.
Set up SIL benchmarks in Gazebo and NVIDIA Isaac Sim, which cut hardware test cycles by 40%.
Packaged the robot software in Docker, so setting up a new machine took 75% less time and every deployment came out the same.
Wrote the platform's technical roadmap and development plan.

experience.title: Robotics Systems Engineer
details: Designed the software stack for the Robo-Cafe product and built a detailed CoppeliaSim simulator for it, which lowered development cost by about 30%.
Connected industrial PLCs to high-level ROS controllers for factory-automation projects.
Set up the company's Git workflow and CI/CD pipeline.

education.title: M.Sc. Mechatronics Engineering
details: Research on on-track tire identification and adaptive nonlinear MPC.

education.title: B.Sc. Mechatronics Engineering
details: Thesis: an autonomous robot arm for non-destructive e-waste disassembly. Developed the approach-and-unscrew algorithm (98% success rate) and screw localisation with YOLOv5 and a depth camera.
Built a 10-method SDK that simplifies MoveIt motion planning and frame transforms, plus a CoppeliaSim / ROS 1 digital twin for testing.

education.title: Robotics Software Engineer Nanodegree
details: Capstone: home-service robot with A*, EKF and PID in C++ / ROS, tested in Gazebo.

projects.title: Formula Student AI Simulator
projects.summary: A configurable CARLA 0.9.16 and Unreal Engine 4.26 simulator for Formula Student AI teams and researchers.
projects.description:
Built between July and August 2026 for Formula Student AI teams and researchers. Sensor placement, parameters and rates are all set in config, so teams can start testing their algorithms right away.

Track: Silverstone, UK.
Vehicle: Formula AI model tuned to approximate real-world vehicle parameters.
details: Built on CARLA 0.9.16 and Unreal Engine 4.26.
Sensor placement, parameters and rates set from a single config.
Vehicle model tuned to approximate the real Formula AI car.

projects.title: On-Track System Identification & Adaptive Nonlinear MPC
projects.summary: Estimates Pacejka tire coefficients on the track with no prior vehicle data, then hands over to nonlinear MPC.
projects.description: Research project on identifying vehicle and tire parameters while driving, and using them in an adaptive nonlinear model predictive controller.
details: Built a pipeline that estimates Pacejka Magic Formula tire coefficients on the track, starting with no prior vehicle data.
Wrote a supervisory controller: the car first drives on Pure Pursuit to gather excitation data, then switches to nonlinear MPC once the parameters are known.
Drove stably on a low-friction surface (µ = 0.35) at up to 100 km/h.

projects.title: Autonomous Agricultural Robot Simulation Stack
projects.summary: A full autonomy stack for a 4WS/4WD agricultural robot in NVIDIA Isaac Sim with the Isaac ROS ecosystem.
projects.description: A full-fidelity simulation stack for an autonomous agricultural robot with Double Ackermann (4WS/4WD) steering. NVIDIA Isaac Sim provides physics-based, photorealistic simulation; Isaac ROS provides GPU-accelerated perception, mapping and navigation.
details: USD-based agricultural environment in NVIDIA Isaac Sim with realistic terrain, HDRI lighting and physics.
Multi-camera ESS stereo disparity and depth estimation on the GPU.
NVIDIA cuVSLAM for GPU-accelerated visual odometry, mapping and relocalisation.
YOLO-based segmentation to mask dynamic objects out of the depth maps.

projects.title: Path-Tracking Controller Benchmark
projects.summary: Pure Pursuit, Stanley and MPC path tracking, compared in CARLA through ROS 2.
projects.description: Implemented three path-tracking controllers in Python and compared how each one follows the same track in CARLA.
details: Implemented Pure Pursuit, Stanley and MPC path tracking.
Ran every controller in CARLA through ROS 2 and compared tracking performance.
Written in Python.

projects.title: Rotary Inverted Pendulum: LQR with Hardware-in-the-Loop
projects.summary: Designed the mechanism, derived its state-space model and balanced it with LQR in Simulink.
projects.description: MATLAB/Simulink and Autodesk Inventor project, from mechanical design to a balanced pendulum on real hardware.
details: Designed the mechanism in Autodesk Inventor.
Derived a state-space model from the nonlinear dynamics.
Balanced the pendulum with LQR in Simulink, with the hardware in the loop.

projects.title: Shell Urban Concept Autonomous Simulator
projects.summary: A Dockerised Gazebo Harmonic and ROS 2 simulator for Shell Eco-marathon teams that runs on low-spec laptops.
projects.description: Built for the Shell Eco-marathon Urban Concept autonomous teams at the Autotronics Research Lab so they can test navigation without the car.
details: Modular simulation framework on ROS 2 Humble and Gazebo Harmonic.
Docker images keep every team member's environment the same.
Integrated sensor models and vehicle dynamics with a multidisciplinary team.
Wrote the documentation and user guides.

projects.title: Self-Driving Car Simulator
projects.summary: A CoppeliaSim simulator of an Ackermann-steering car with ROS 1, built for the Egyptian EV Rally.
projects.description: A simulation of the competition car built from the ground up, used by the teams in the Egyptian Electric Vehicle Rally.
details: Modelled the Ackermann-steering car in SolidWorks and converted it to URDF.
Tuned the physics to a 10% sim-to-real error.
Added 3D LiDAR, IMU and GPS, and connected the scene to ROS 1 through Lua.

projects.title: ABB IRB 120 Simulator
projects.summary: ROS 1 and MoveIt connected to CoppeliaSim for an industrial arm. Cited in a Master's thesis in Italy.
projects.description: A simulator for the ABB IRB 120 industrial arm. The simulator bridge was cited in a Master's thesis in Italy.
details: Integrated ROS 1 and MoveIt with CoppeliaSim.
Designed the complete simulation environment for the robot.

projects.title: Autonomous E-Waste Disassembly Arm
projects.summary: B.Sc. thesis: a robot arm that removes screws from e-waste without damaging it, at a 98% success rate.
projects.description: Graduation project on non-destructive disassembly of electronic waste with a robot arm.
details: Developed the approach-and-unscrew algorithm, reaching a 98% success rate.
Localised screws with YOLOv5 and a depth camera.
Built a 10-method SDK that simplifies MoveIt motion planning and frame transforms.
Designed a software architecture that coordinates 11 algorithms.
Tested everything on a CoppeliaSim / ROS 1 digital twin.
